title: Attaching an extreme mapping bimodule in a directed category
statement:
Use small simplicial categories, weak homotopy equivalences and the Bergner model structure of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Let $I$ be a finite linearly ordered set with distinct least and greatest elements $a<b$, let $(O_i)_{i\in I}$ be disjoint small sets, and let $S\subseteq I$ contain $a,b$. A category directed by these blocks has the indicated object set and has empty mapping sets from $O_j$ to $O_i$ when $i<j$. Let $B$ be directed on $I$, and let $T,V$ be directed on $S$. Let $g:T\to B$ and $f:T\to V$ be enriched functors preserving the block labels, equal on objects to the inclusion and identity respectively. Suppose that $f:T(u,v)\to V(u,v)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence unless $u\in O_a,v\in O_b$. Suppose also that $g$ induces weak homotopy equivalences on all mapping sets within $O_a$ and within $O_b$.

There are a directed simplicial-category diagram $V'$ on the same $S$-blocks and natural enriched functors $j:T\to V'$ and $p:V'\to V$ with $f=j\circ p$, such that every component $p$ is a Bergner weak homotopy equivalence and $V'$ has the same labelled object sets as $V$. For every strict cocone $B\xleftarrow{g}T\xrightarrow{j}V'$ which is a Bergner homotopy pushout, the canonical square through $V'(x,z)$ is a homotopy pushout of spaces for $x\in O_a,z\in O_b$, and the map $V'(x,z)\to V(x,z)$ induced by $p$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. The cocone map from $B$ is a weak homotopy equivalence on every other mapping set. A representative of this strict homotopy-pushout cocone has object set $\coprod_{i\in I}O_i$, and all comparisons are natural for maps of such diagrams preserving blocks and cocones. Empty blocks and mapping sets are allowed, and no local Kan hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text:
First record the effect of one boundary-arrow cell in a category $C$ directed on the given blocks. Attach $U(K)\to U(L)$ at $u\in O_a,v\in O_b$, where $K=\partial\Delta^n$, $L=\Delta^n$. In the word-filtration formula, words containing at least two new letters have a factor $C(v,u)=\varnothing$, so only lengths zero and one remain. The coefficient for the length-one words from $w$ to $z$ is
$$H_C(w,z)=C(v,z)\times C(w,u).$$
It is empty unless $w\in O_a,z\in O_b$: a block before $a$ or after $b$ would otherwise be necessary. Thus all other mapping sets, including both endpoint full subcategories, are unchanged, and the remaining mapping set is exactly
$$C^+(w,z)=C(w,z)\amalg_{H_C(w,z)\times K}(H_C(w,z)\times L).$$
The old-to-new maps are monomorphisms. These assertions are the length-one specialization of [lem-coef-scat-arrow-cell-word-filtration], not an assertion that enriched pushouts are generally computed mappingwise. The fixed-object and variable-object attachments agree by [lem-coef-scat-fixed-object-pushout-comparison]. Both formulas retain the actual composition attaching maps.

proof.text: Put $O=\coprod_{i\in S}O_i$. Work in $\mathrm{sCat}_O$ with the model structure of [lem-coef-fixed-object-simplicial-free-calculus]. For $u\in O_a,v\in O_b,n\geq0$ take the set $J$ of maps $F^O_{u,v}(\partial\Delta^n)\to F^O_{u,v}(\Delta^n)$ from [lem-coef-fixed-object-free-arrow-adjunction]. The smallness hypothesis for [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization] holds with $\kappa=\aleph_0$. Indeed a filtered colimit with fixed objects has the degreewise filtered colimits as mapping sets: compose two represented arrows at a common stage; independence and the associative and unit equations hold at a later common stage. This constructs the colimit and verifies its universal property. Evaluation therefore preserves these colimits. By the displayed free/evaluation adjunction, maps from a domain in $J$ are maps from the finite simplicial set $\partial\Delta^n$ into that evaluation. Finitely many nondegenerate simplices and finitely many face equations factor, and become equal, at a common stage. Hence this Hom functor preserves the required chains, including $n=0$ with empty boundary. All sets of generators and attaching squares are small after the fixed universe enlargement.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization] to $f:T\to V$ and $J$, obtaining $T\xrightarrow{j}V'\xrightarrow{p}V$ with $j$ a $J$-cell map and $p$ having the right lifting property against $J$. Write the continuous cellular sequence as $(T_\alpha)$, with $T_0=T$ and $T_\theta=V'$. The standard construction attaches all commutative generator squares at each stage; the compactness just checked allows countably many stages. Each generator is a fixed-object cofibration: by adjunction, its lifting problem against a local trivial Kan fibration is a boundary-lifting problem. It is consequently a Bergner cofibration by [lem-coef-fixed-object-simplicial-free-calculus]; equivalently the attachment comparison and the boundary-arrow generators of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting] give the same assertion. The cellular left factor has the corresponding left lifting property, so $j$ is a Bergner cofibration. Step 1, applied successively, says that every $T_\alpha$ is directed and that $j$ is the identity on every nonextreme mapping set. Filtered colimits here are the mappingwise colimits verified in step 2.

proof.text: For $u\in O_a,v\in O_b$, the free/evaluation adjunction converts the lifting property of $p$ into the right lifting property of $V'(u,v)\to V(u,v)$ against every boundary inclusion. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] it is a trivial Kan fibration, hence a weak homotopy equivalence. On every other mapping set $V'$ equals $T$, so $p$ there is $f$, a weak homotopy equivalence by hypothesis. The functor $p$ is identity on objects, so its mappingwise equivalences also give essential surjectivity. It is thus a Dwyer--Kan equivalence by [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. In particular this replacement of $V$ neither assumes nor produces a local Kan hypothesis on the original data.

proof.text: Let $B_\alpha=B\amalg_T T_\alpha$, with the functor from $T_\alpha$ given by the pushout cocone; put $P=B_\theta$. At a successor this attaches exactly the same arrow cells to $B_\alpha$ as to $T_\alpha$. This follows from the universal property: giving a functor out of either iterated pushout is giving a functor out of $B$ and one out of the enlarged $T_\alpha$ agreeing on $T$. A coproduct of cells may be well ordered and attached one at a time, with the same universal property at its end. No new objects occur in any such attachment (step 1). Hence $B_\alpha$ has object set $\coprod_{i\in I}O_i$, is directed, and its nonextreme mapping sets are exactly those of $B$. Its full endpoint subcategories remain $B|_{O_a}$ and $B|_{O_b}$. At limits the same statements follow from the mappingwise filtered-colimit construction of step 2.

source.place: Paragraph 2, inherited coherent coefficient-adjunction foundation; Q43 supplies the extreme-arrow cellular argument, using the existing enriched free-arrow and model-colimit nodes. This auxiliary assertion is not a numbered theorem in the blueprint or HTT.

proof.text: The ordinary pushout $P=B\amalg_T V'$ computes the Bergner homotopy pushout. In fact this model structure is left proper by [lem-coef-scat-bergner-left-proper-pushouts], is locally presentable with functorial small-object factorizations for the sets $I$ and $J$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting], and it is combinatorial. Indeed that statement characterizes $J$-inj exactly as the Bergner fibrations of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], so the trivial cofibrations, having the left lifting property against them, are $J$-cof. By adjunction and the boundary characterization of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], $I$-inj consists of the object-surjective functors that are trivial Kan fibrations on every mapping set. Such a functor is a local Kan fibration and a Dwyer--Kan equivalence, being bijective on components of mapping sets and surjective on objects. It lifts equivalence vertices: lift the target object, then the vertex, which stays invertible because $\pi_0$ of the functor is fully faithful. Conversely, a trivial Bergner fibration is locally a trivial Kan fibration. It is surjective on objects: given $b$, essential surjectivity gives some $pa\to b$ invertible in $\pi_0$, and equivalence lifting gives an $a'$ with $pa'=b$. Hence the trivial fibrations are $I$-inj and the cofibrations are $I$-cof. Moreover $j:T\to V'$ is a cofibration by step 3. Thus comparison (a) of [lem-cbc-left-proper-derived-cell-colimits] applies, without assuming $T$, $B$ or $V'$ cofibrant. The map of spans $(B\leftarrow T\to V')\to(B\leftarrow T\to V)$ is an objectwise weak equivalence by step 4. The projective derived-colimit comparison [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison] identifies their homotopy pushout cocones. Consequently $P$ represents the stated $Z$, with the original cocone after inverting $p$. Its labelled objects are the original ones. All mapping-space assertions can therefore be checked on $P$ and its cocone. These are equivalences of labelled cocones.

proof.text:
Fix $x\in O_a,z\in O_b$. Define simplicial sets and their actual comparison maps
$$R_\alpha=B(x,z)\amalg_{T(x,z)}T_\alpha(x,z),\qquad r_\alpha:R_\alpha\to B_\alpha(x,z).$$
The map $r_\alpha$ is induced by the two composition-preserving cocone maps. We prove by cellular induction that it is a weak homotopy equivalence. At $\alpha=0$, it is the identity of $B(x,z)$. For a single next cell at $(u,v)$ define
$$H_T=T(v,z)\times T(x,u),\qquad H_B=B(v,z)\times B(x,u).$$
Both factors lie within endpoint blocks. They remain unchanged throughout both sequences by steps 1 and 5, so these formulas are valid at every stage. The map $H_T\to H_B$ is the product of the original two maps induced by $g$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, inherited coherent coefficient-adjunction foundation; Q43 supplies the extreme-arrow cellular argument, using the existing enriched free-arrow and model-colimit nodes. This auxiliary assertion is not a numbered theorem in the blueprint or HTT.

proof.text: By the hypothesis on $g$, the two factors in $H_T\to H_B$ are weak homotopy equivalences. Their product, and its product with $K$ or $L$, are weak homotopy equivalences. For completeness, [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits] identifies the realization of a finite simplicial product with the product in k-spaces. Components of a finite product are pairs of components and, at a paired basepoint, sphere maps and their homotopies into a product are pairs. Hence all homotopy groups are products of the corresponding homotopy groups. The weak-equivalence definition in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] now gives the assertion, also if a factor is empty. No fibrant replacement of a mapping set is used here.

proof.text:
By step 1 and the ordinary pushout universal property, the next $R$ is
$$R_{\alpha+1}=R_\alpha\amalg_{H_T\times K}(H_T\times L),$$
where the attaching map is through $T_\alpha(x,z)$, whereas
$$B_{\alpha+1}(x,z)=B_\alpha(x,z)\amalg_{H_B\times K}(H_B\times L).$$
The evident map of these spans commutes because the attaching squares were pushed forward by the functor $T_\alpha\to B_\alpha$, which preserves composition. Its three component maps are weak homotopy equivalences: the map of old terms is $r_\alpha$ by induction, and the two coefficient maps are from step 8. Both maps $H_T\times K\to H_T\times L$ and $H_B\times K\to H_B\times L$ are monomorphisms degreewise. Apply the pushout assertion of [lem-coef-sset-gluing-filtered-equivalences] to obtain that $r_{\alpha+1}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. This proves the successor step, also through the one-cell refinement of a family of attachments.

proof.text:
At a nonzero limit $\beta$, step 2 gives $T_\beta(x,z)=\operatorname{colim}_{\alpha<\beta}T_\alpha(x,z)$ and $B_\beta(x,z)=\operatorname{colim}_{\alpha<\beta}B_\alpha(x,z)$. The definition of $R$ commutes with this colimit: maps from either side to a test simplicial set are a map from $B(x,z)$ and compatible maps from all $T_\alpha(x,z)$, agreeing on $T(x,z)$. Thus $r_\beta$ is the filtered colimit of the maps $r_\alpha$. The ordinal is nonempty and directed, so the filtered-colimit clause of [lem-coef-sset-gluing-filtered-equivalences] proves it is a weak homotopy equivalence. In particular
$$B(x,z)\amalg_{T(x,z)}V'(x,z)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }P(x,z).$$
This is the comparison from the original mapping-space cocone; its maps from the two terms were kept throughout the induction.

source.place: Paragraph 2, inherited coherent coefficient-adjunction foundation; Q43 supplies the extreme-arrow cellular argument, using the existing enriched free-arrow and model-colimit nodes. This auxiliary assertion is not a numbered theorem in the blueprint or HTT.

proof.text: The map $T(x,z)\to V'(x,z)$ is a monomorphism, since each cell was a monomorphism by step 1 and a continuous union of monomorphisms is a monomorphism degreewise. All simplicial sets are cofibrant by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Therefore the ordinary pushout in step 10 is a homotopy pushout of spaces: compare a cofibrant replacement of its span to the original span using assertion (b) of [lem-coef-model-cofibrant-colimit-comparison]. All six objects are cofibrant and the distinguished legs are cofibrations, as that assertion requires. Combining the weak equivalence in step 10 with $V'(x,z)\to V(x,z)$ from step 4 identifies the whole square with the square in the statement, using the cocone comparison in step 6. On every other mapping set $B\to P$ is the identity by step 5, hence a weak homotopy equivalence. This also proves the object-set assertion for the representative $P$.

proof.text: Finally retain maps of diagrams. Choose the small-object construction of step 3 by attaching every generator square, rather than choosing individual fillers. A block-preserving map sends the square at $(u,v,n)$ to its image square at the image objects, even if it identifies objects. The finite-word construction of the free-arrow functor in [lem-coef-fixed-object-free-arrow-adjunction] supplies the induced maps of attaching objects. This gives maps of the cellular sequences by induction and by the colimit universal property at limits; the countable-stage choice in step 3 is uniform. Word reduction, the two cocone inclusions defining $r_\alpha$, and the coefficient maps are natural by [lem-coef-scat-arrow-cell-word-filtration]. The derived-colimit comparisons of [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison] preserve the cocones and their maps. Hence all comparisons just established are natural after the stipulated weak equivalences are inverted. Empty endpoint blocks give an empty generator family and no extreme pairs to check; an empty individual mapping set is allowed in every cell and every product above.

Steps 2–5 are right: compactness with κ=ℵ0, the restricted free-cell factorization, p a local trivial fibration at the extreme pairs and equal to f elsewhere, and B_α=B⊔_T T_α. Steps 7–11 are right: a cellular induction using the gluing and filtered clauses with monomorphism legs, step 8 giving H_T→H_B as a weak equivalence by the endpoint hypothesis, and clause (b) of the cofibrant-colimit node in sSet. One C3/C4 fault was in step 6. Clause (a) of the tool lemma needs a combinatorial model category, but lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting does not state that I-inj equals the trivial Bergner fibrations. I wrote out that identification and the J-cof argument, adding coherent-nerve-comparison and kan-quillen-right-proper to the step's uses (both were already in proof_deps); the corrected item is under fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors/. statement_change.old_statement:
Use small simplicial categories, weak homotopy equivalences and the Bergner model structure of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Let $I$ be a finite linearly ordered set with distinct least and greatest elements $a<b$, let $(O_i)_{i\in I}$ be disjoint small sets, and let $S\subseteq I$ contain $a,b$. A category directed by these blocks has the indicated object set and has empty mapping sets from $O_j$ to $O_i$ when $i<j$. Let $B$ be directed on $I$, and let $T,V$ be directed on $S$. Let $g:T\to B$ and $f:T\to V$ be enriched functors preserving the block labels, equal on objects to the inclusion and identity respectively. Suppose that $f:T(u,v)\to V(u,v)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence unless $u\in O_a,v\in O_b$. Suppose also that $g$ induces weak homotopy equivalences on all mapping sets within $O_a$ and within $O_b$.

For the homotopy pushout $Z=B\amalg_T^h V$ in the Bergner model structure, with its specified cocone maps, the canonical square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}T(x,z)&\longrightarrow&V(x,z)\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ B(x,z)&\longrightarrow&Z(x,z)\end{array}$$
is a homotopy pushout of spaces for $x\in O_a,z\in O_b$. Here homotopy pushouts mean derived colimits of the respective spans, with their maps. The cocone map $B\to Z$ induces a weak homotopy equivalence on every other mapping set. The object set of a representative of $Z$ can be taken to be $\coprod_{i\in I}O_i$. All comparisons are natural for maps of such diagrams preserving blocks and cocones. Empty blocks and mapping sets are allowed, and no local Kan hypothesis is imposed.
statement_change.what: The original existential conjunct required a strict homotopy-pushout cocone for the given map f:T→V. This is false: for I={a<b}, O_a={x}, O_b={z}, T(x,z)=S⁰, T(x,x)=T(z,z)=pt, T(z,x)=∅, and B=V=[1] with g=f the collapse, the ordinary pushout is [1] while the homotopy-pushout mapping space is S¹, so no such strict cocone over f exists. The corrected statement uses the cellular factorization f=j≫p with p a componentwise Bergner weak equivalence and asserts the strict cocone and mapping square for j, together with the weak equivalence V′(x,z)→V(x,z).
